body: Pocky & Rocky is Natsume's Super Nintendo action game about a shrine maiden and a tanuki fighting through a world of monsters inspired by Japanese folklore. Pocky throws paper talismans, while Rocky attacks with leaves. One or two players guide the pair through stages viewed from above, approaching enemies from different directions rather than following a fixed firing lane. Their expressive animation and unusual opponents give the journey a playful character, even when the screen becomes crowded and staying alive demands a carefully chosen movement.

Both characters combine ranged attacks with a close defensive action, making distance part of the decision at every encounter. A target can be attacked from safety, but an incoming projectile may call for an immediate response nearby. Sliding provides another movement option when the surrounding threats become difficult to avoid. Two players can divide their attention between different enemies, though sharing the same space also requires awareness of the other person's position. Cooperation works best when the partners create room for each other to move.

The game continues the world introduced by Taito's Kiki Kaikai, reworking it through Natsume's characters and cooperative console action. Temples, shrines and eccentric bosses make the setting recognisable without interrupting the next shooting challenge. Hiroyuki Iwatsuki composed the score. Released in Japan in 1992 and overseas in 1993, it established the Pocky & Rocky name used for the home-console adventures. The memorable partnership gives the familiar work of moving, shooting and avoiding danger a personality that belongs to the two figures sharing the screen.
